summary.text:
Within these results, Oatly's frontier candidates are cooking and food culture and feminism and women's voices, both on partial routes with medium evidence quality and no relative position against a comparison set. British and London urban culture and folk and indie music have no usable evidence yet, so they cannot be assessed. No candidate has a robustness level, so any expansion read rests only on shared signals and brand-conditioned association, and these results cannot say whether any territory would be a credible expansion for Oatly.
Cooking and food culture: Filtered shared signals for this territory's book exemplars (indie, female protagonist, lesbian) fall in a SOME band, suggesting a loose rather than tight shared profile. The brand-conditioned query returned a supported list whose leading titles center on food history, class and cooking science, indicating association with food culture rather than a ranked fit. Evidence quality is medium and the route is partial, so the food-culture association is an exploratory signal rather than a settled finding.
Feminism and women's voices: Shared signals (electronic, indie, musician, female protagonist, lesbian) fall in a SOME band, pointing to a loosely shared profile with music-adjacent overlap. The brand-conditioned query returned a supported list whose top entries lean toward women in space, science and exercise history, an association pattern rather than a ranked fit. Evidence quality is medium on a partial route with no relative position, so the association should be treated as provisional.
British and London urban culture: No concept anchors this territory and the route is insufficient evidence, so no cultural association can be described from these results.
Folk and indie music: Folk has only a descriptive concept without a validated exemplar panel, so its route cannot yet support any association claim.

followUpOptions: Build a comparison set for cooking and food culture with additional book exemplars to enable a relative position.
Validate an exemplar panel for folk and indie music so its representation can support analysis.
Probe London, England with venue or book entity types to test whether British and London urban culture can be anchored.
Widen the brand-conditioned list for feminism and women's voices beyond the truncated top entries to check whether the association holds.

agentInterpretation.summary:
Within these results, Oatly's frontier candidates are cooking and food culture and feminism and women's voices, both on partial routes with medium evidence quality and no relative position against a comparison set. British and London urban culture and folk and indie music have no usable evidence yet, so they cannot be assessed. No candidate has a robustness level, so any expansion read rests only on shared signals and brand-conditioned association, and these results cannot say whether any territory would be a credible expansion for Oatly.
Cooking and food culture: Filtered shared signals for this territory's book exemplars (indie, female protagonist, lesbian) fall in a SOME band, suggesting a loose rather than tight shared profile. The brand-conditioned query returned a supported list whose leading titles center on food history, class and cooking science, indicating association with food culture rather than a ranked fit. Evidence quality is medium and the route is partial, so the food-culture association is an exploratory signal rather than a settled finding.
Feminism and women's voices: Shared signals (electronic, indie, musician, female protagonist, lesbian) fall in a SOME band, pointing to a loosely shared profile with music-adjacent overlap. The brand-conditioned query returned a supported list whose top entries lean toward women in space, science and exercise history, an association pattern rather than a ranked fit. Evidence quality is medium on a partial route with no relative position, so the association should be treated as provisional.
British and London urban culture: No concept anchors this territory and the route is insufficient evidence, so no cultural association can be described from these results.
Folk and indie music: Folk has only a descriptive concept without a validated exemplar panel, so its route cannot yet support any association claim.
